about: Generated by scripts/catalog.py from the library's folders. Do not edit: the check fails if it differs.

hooks.name: head.styles
hooks.about: the page head, after the core stylesheet: link tags for a plugin's own stylesheet, a <style> of its settings, and a small same-origin script that must run before the first paint (time-of-day sets html[data-daypart]); never an inline script

hooks.name: header.topbar
hooks.about: the top bar of the header (the nearest-campfire slot on S'mores); the core's default is used when no plugin fills it

hooks.name: body.end
hooks.about: markup and script tags at the end of every page, just before </body> (the Talk bubble); empty when no plugin fills it

filters.name: page.html
filters.about: a finished page's HTML, each plugin's output the next one's input (content-blocks marks {{namespace:name}} here)

plugins.name: agent-files
plugins.about: What an agent reads on a Pages site (herdos public-site rules 6 and 7): a markdown twin of every page, built after the site's build and served on Accept: text/markdown; the agent card's /a2a endpoint, which refuses plainly until the site has chat; and a read-only MCP at /mcp that lists the sitemap's pages and returns one page's twin. Public pages only, no auth, no writes. The site writes its own agent-card.json and mcp.json, with the MCP server card, api-catalog, skills index, ard.json and ai-catalog.json, through site-templates' discovery.py (site-kit#314).

plugins.name: content-blocks
plugins.about: Company details written once and changed without a deploy. A page holds {{company:copyright}}; the build bakes in the current value from data/blocks.json, marked as a content block, and as the page is served the edge swaps each block's text for the value in one KV document. Nothing in KV (or KV down) leaves the baked value, so a visitor never sees a placeholder.

plugins.name: hero-character
plugins.about: A character standing in a page's hero, with a speech bubble of real text. Both sit in front of the hero's own background (time-of-day's skyline, when a site uses it) and never behind its copy. The line is in the built page, so it reads with no script, and the bubble's fill makes it readable over any background. On phones the character and the bubble follow the hero's copy.

plugins.name: hero-scenes
plugins.about: Canvas hero animations for the kit's .hero-anim slot: flow (business info streams into a site and out to AI answer cards), orb, answer, blocks, pins and page. One small engine with no library. Decoration only: the canvas is aria-hidden and the words stay in the page's HTML. Each scene keeps the slot's rules: no layout shift, it runs only while on screen and the tab is visible, reduced motion gets one still frame. Colours come from the site's own tokens; the assistant names, the other words, the font and which scenes may run come from the settings. A site adds its own scene with register().

scenes.default: flow, orb, answer, blocks, pins, page

assistants.default: AI search, AI chat, AI answers

cited.default: yourbusiness.com: cited in the answer | cited in the answer

plugins.name: link-rotator
plugins.about: One card that shows one set of up to four links at a time (a title and its links) and turns to the next set every few seconds. Small tabs under the title show which set is up and let a person pick one; picking, or the Pause button, stops the turning; it also waits while the pointer is over the card or focus is inside it. With reduced motion set nothing turns. A screen reader hears the set a person chose, never a change every few seconds. Without script the first set shows.

plugins.name: location-picker
plugins.about: Puts the nearest campfire in the header, with a no-JavaScript picker. The edge code picks the place from the visitor's region for one request and keeps nothing; a visitor who picks one gets a cookie holding the place's slug.

plugins.name: map
plugins.about: A real, zoomable map for a site's own places (site-kit#64): pan and zoom, pins that group when they crowd and split as you zoom in, a card for each pin that links to its page, and a layer filter. The page marks where it goes with <!--site-kit:map--> and the site hands the plugin its pins (each page's lat and lng) as ctx.map. Tiles are vector tiles from OpenFreeMap (free, no key, no cookies, public sites allowed), drawn by MapLibre GL JS 5.24.0 vendored in the plugin and never loaded from a CDN, and recoloured to the site's own colours. The pins are real buttons, MapLibre's keyboard pan and zoom stay on, and a plain list of every place sits under the map, so a screen reader, a search engine and a browser with no JavaScript get everything. The library loads only on a page with the map, once the map is near the screen.

plugins.name: monthly-edition
plugins.about: A masthead that turns over on the 1st by itself, like a monthly comic: "Vol. 1, Issue #2 · December 2026", that month's cover line and its palette, from the site's own data/editions.json. The build bakes in the month it runs, so a page with no script reads right as of its build; a small same-origin script in the head picks the visitor's local month from the entries the build embedded, so the 1st turns it over with no redeploy. A month with no entry keeps the latest one before it. It reads the local clock only and sends nothing anywhere.

plugins.name: paypal-button
plugins.about: One PayPal Standard button (an _xclick form) per configured item: dues, an event fee, a workshop seat, a donation. Every value comes from the site's config, with no default amount, currency, item, button text or brand, and the build refuses a config missing any of them. sandbox is explicit: true posts to PayPal's sandbox, false (set on purpose) to the live site, and a config without it is refused. Plain markup, every value attribute-escaped, no script. `plugin.py render --config <file>` prints the form, the one source for a hand-placed copy. The posted form is never trusted: the site's IPN listener verifies with PayPal and checks receiver, amount, currency and item against its own config.

plugins.name: preview-feedback
plugins.about: Click-to-comment pins on a site's branch preview deploys: a reviewer signs in through the site agent, each pin is kept in D1 and the agent posts it on the branch's open pull request, naming the person, with the page, the element and a screenshot link. It does nothing on production.

plugins.name: quickfind
plugins.about: A quick-find box on ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux): type to find a page from the site's own index (its llms.txt, or a sitemap), Enter goes there, Esc closes. Works by keyboard alone and with a screen reader (a dialog with a combobox and a listbox). Where the page has the Talk bubble, the last row asks the host instead. Nothing loads until the first ⌘K, and then only the site's own index file; nothing is sent anywhere.

plugins.name: radar
plugins.about: Cookieless page views for Foo's Radar. Each page view sends the page address without its query string and only the referring site's name (its origin) to the site's own /api/radar. The edge passes that on to the site's Radar collector together with the visitor's IP address and browser user agent, which the collector uses only in memory, to count unique visitors per day and to work out a device type, and never stores. The collector keeps the page address without its query string, the referring site's name only, and the device type. No cookies, no browser storage, no IP address stored, nothing stored that identifies a visitor. Sends nothing when the browser asks not to be tracked (Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track). Holds no key: only the name of the setting that holds it.

plugins.name: sitemap-check
plugins.about: A build check for a site deployed to Cloudflare Pages: every URL its sitemap lists must be served as listed, with no redirect (an .html URL, the wrong trailing slash, a _redirects source), no noindex, nothing missing and no other origin. It reads the built folder after the build, with no network, and fails the build naming each URL and its reason.

plugins.name: talk
plugins.about: A host a visitor can talk to, by text or voice, answering only from the site's own data. A campfire bubble, bottom-right, opens a chat panel (text first, a voice button inside); it shows only when GET /api/talk-status says Talk is on. The edge: a short-lived ElevenLabs session, a text chat through a provider fallback chain (Ollama, Gemini after a credit failure, Workers AI, OpenRouter, then a visible retry, never a canned answer) and a per-visitor limit in KV. Holds no key: only the names of the settings and bindings.

plugins.name: theme-picker
plugins.about: A visitor picks one of a site's looks (its variants: colours, fonts, images and time-of-day skylines) from a small menu, and the choice stays in their own browser. The default variant is baked in, so a page with no script, and a visitor who never picks, sees the site as it is. A small same-origin script in the head sets html[data-variant] from the saved choice before the first paint, so there is no flash. The choice lives only in the visitor's localStorage and is never sent anywhere.

plugins.name: time-of-day
plugins.about: A backdrop that follows the visitor's local time: up to four images (dawn, day, dusk, night) behind one element the site names, each with its own darkening scrim so the text on it stays readable. The right one shows from the first paint, only that image loads, and it cross-fades if the daypart changes while the page is open (no fade with reduced motion). Without script, the day image shows. It reads the local clock only and sends nothing anywhere.

plugins.name: waitlist
plugins.about: A waitlist sign-up form that works with no JavaScript: a person leaves an email address and, if they like, their site's address, and the site keeps them in its own Cloudflare D1 database. Each sign-up is kept only after Cloudflare Turnstile says a person sent it from this site. A new address, an address already on the list and a bot that fills the hidden trap field all get the same thank-you page, so the form never tells anyone who is on the list. Nothing a person types is ever logged or put in a page address. Holds no key: only the name of the setting that holds the Turnstile secret.

plugins.name: webmcp
plugins.about: A site's real tools, registered with the browser's WebMCP API (document.modelContext.registerTool) so an agent in the browser can call them. Each tool posts its input as JSON to the endpoint its form already uses and returns the answer as text content. Only where the browser has the API: no polyfill, nothing new server-side. The tools come from a webmcp block in the site's agent config (the file discovery.py reads); a build step after the site's build writes the one script with the tools inlined and adds it to the pages the block names. A tool with no endpoint, name, description or object inputSchema, or an endpoint that does not answer, stops the build.

skills.name: blog-writer
skills.description: Write a site's blog posts in nine steps (topic queue, brief, research, persona by beat, draft, edit, fact-check that opens every cited URL, scored review and gate, schedule and PR), with blog_writer.py for the code parts and run.py to run it unattended.

skills.name: brand
skills.description: Give a site its brand as one record (.sitekit/brand.json), checked by brand.py --check, with brand.py --leak proving a white-label tenant's build shows nothing of the first brand.

skills.name: site-kit
skills.description: Check the site-kit catalog before building anything on one of Seth's sites, and open a plugin proposal for anything new.

skills.name: site-templates
skills.description: Build a site from a template, a layout record of blocks made only of WordPress core-block parts, checked whole by layout.py, so one source renders as a static site and exports as a block theme.

skills.name: style-guide
skills.description: Give a site its style guide in S'mores' shape: canon/STYLEGUIDE.md for the words, a brand assets folder, and a /style-guide/ page generated from the canon by style_guide.py.

services.name: short-links
services.about: Short links on a site's own short domain, in the spirit of Pretty Links and Lasso (site-kit#186): the bare domain goes to the site, and each code redirects (301, 302 or 307) to its target, with nofollow and sponsored sent as X-Robots-Tag and the query passed through when asked. Clicks are counted per code per day in the service's D1: total, unique visitors, the referring site's name and the country. No raw IP stored and no cookie. A unique visitor is a salted hash kept for one UTC day: the salt is random each day and is in the same database, so for that day a hash is pseudonymous, not anonymous; a daily job deletes the past day's salt and hashes. The site's owner reads its own counts from GET /api/counts on the short domain, with the site's read token.
